headline: The Sport Fishing Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a fishing partner a technique and check it back, solve a broken boat or bait shortage with your captain, give feedback and settle disputes in your group, report an injury, near miss or safety call, and write a clear tag report or trip message in Spanish.

lessons.title: Explain Why We Chase Bait Before First Light
lessons.objective: Explain the morning's sequence and the reason for each step, then check your partner's teach-back.

words.note: Common Mexican word for a hand-thrown cast net.
Loanword used on the boats; say sa-BEE-kee.
An offshore shoal or high spot where game fish gather.
Masculine when it means sequence; the feminine form means a command.

words.en: First we look for bait, then we run to the bank.
words.es: Primero buscamos carnada, luego corremos al banco.

words.en: We leave early because at dawn the bait is close to shore.
words.es: Salimos temprano porque al amanecer la carnada está cerca de la orilla.

words.en: That's why we don't run to the bank without having bait.
words.es: Por eso no corremos al banco sin tener carnada.

words.en: Then, when the sun comes up, we start fishing.
words.es: Después, cuando sale el sol, empezamos a pescar.

words.en: Lucía, can you explain the plan in your own words?
words.es: Lucía, ¿me explicas el plan con tus palabras?
words.note: Informal (tú) with a friend.

words.en: And why do you think we go to the point first?
words.es: ¿Y por qué crees que vamos primero a la punta?
words.note: Informal check question for the teach-back.

words.en: Captain, will you correct me if I get the order wrong?
words.es: Capitán, ¿me corrige si me equivoco en el orden?
words.note: Formal (usted) with the captain.

words.en: You're right, Captain, I got that step wrong.
words.es: Tiene razón, capitán, me equivoqué en ese paso.
words.note: Formal (usted).

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Lucía, a first-time angler: explain the morning plan step by step with primero, luego and después, give the reason for each step with porque and por eso, then ask her to explain it back.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero buscamos carnada, luego corremos al banco, porque..., por eso...)

examples.es: Primero buscamos carnada en la punta y luego corremos al banco.
examples.en: First we look for bait at the point and then we run to the bank.

examples.es: La carnada viva atrae más peces, por eso salimos antes del amanecer.
examples.en: Live bait draws more fish, so that's why we leave before dawn.

lessons.title: Teach a Teen Why Circle Hooks Need No Hard Hook Set
lessons.objective: Teach why circle hooks need a slow pickup instead of a hard hook set, and have a teen explain it back.

words.note: Where a circle hook sets when you let the fish run.
Mexican usage; from the verb jalar, to pull.
Common Mexican form; the textbook form is supervivencia.
Feminine form to agree with the word for line.

words.en: With this hook you don't pull hard.
words.es: Con este anzuelo no se jala fuerte.

words.en: If you pull hard, the hook comes out.
words.es: Si se jala fuerte, se sale el anzuelo.

words.en: You let it run a few seconds and then you tighten the drag.
words.es: Se deja correr unos segundos y luego se aprieta el freno.

words.en: If the line gets tight, you lift the rod slowly.
words.es: Si la línea se pone tensa, se levanta la caña despacio.

words.en: The sardine is hooked through the nose or the back.
words.es: La sardina se engancha por la nariz o por el lomo.

words.en: Mateo, it's okay, everybody loses the first one.
words.es: Mateo, no pasa nada, a todos se nos va el primero.
words.note: Informal (tú) with a teen.

words.en: Why do you think it came off?
words.es: ¿Por qué crees que se te salió?
words.note: Informal; lets him find the mistake himself.

words.en: Rubén, how would you explain it to him?
words.note: Formal (usted) with the mate.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Mateo, a 15-year-old learning to fish live bait on circle hooks: explain the slow pickup with impersonal se (se deja correr) and the rules with si + present (si se jala fuerte, se sale), then have him explain it back.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se deja correr; si se jala fuerte, se sale el anzuelo)

examples.es: Si se jala fuerte, el anzuelo se sale de la boca.
examples.en: If you yank hard, the hook comes out of the mouth.

examples.es: Si se aprieta el freno despacio, el anzuelo se clava en la comisura.
examples.en: If you tighten the drag slowly, the hook sets in the corner of the mouth.

lessons.title: Coach Your Sister-in-Law Through Her First Tuna Fight
lessons.objective: Coach a beginner through a tuna fight with clear commands and have her repeat the line-safety rules.

words.note: From the verb bombear: lift the rod, then reel down.
Mexican usage for a cut on the skin.
Used when a tuna circles under the boat near the end of the fight.

words.en: Lift it slowly and reel on the way down.
words.note: The pronoun refers to the rod. Informal (tú).

words.en: Pump it with your legs, not your back.
words.es: Bombéala con las piernas, no con la espalda.

words.en: Don't touch it; Fernando handles that line.
words.es: No la toques; esa línea la agarra Fernando.

words.en: Never wrap it around your hand.
words.es: Nunca te la enrolles en la mano.

words.en: Rest a little, but don't give it slack.
words.es: Descansa un poco, pero no le aflojes.

words.en: Tell me the two line rules again.
words.es: Dime otra vez las dos reglas de la línea.
words.note: Informal teach-back check.

words.en: Fernando, will you grab the leader when it gets here?
words.es: Fernando, ¿usted agarra el líder cuando llegue?
words.note: Formal (usted) with the mate.

words.en: Very good, that's how it's done, you almost have it.
words.es: Muy bien, así se hace, ya casi lo tienes.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Mariana, your sister-in-law on her first tuna: coach her through the fight with commands like súbela and bombéala despacio, then have her repeat the line-safety rules: no la toques, no te la enrolles en la mano.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (súbela, bombéala despacio, no la toques, no te la enrolles en la mano)

examples.es: Bombéala despacio y recoge cuando bajes la caña.
examples.en: Pump it slowly and reel when you lower the rod.

examples.es: No la toques; deja que Fernando agarre el líder.
examples.en: Don't touch it; let Fernando grab the leader.

lessons.title: Read the Billfish Tag Card Before the Sailfish Comes Up
lessons.objective: Read a tagging program card aloud and explain each step to your partner before the billfish reaches the boat.

words.note: Everyday word on the boat; branquias is the technical term.
For a woman, use the feminine form ending in -a.

words.en: The card says we have to keep it in the water.
words.es: La tarjeta dice que hay que dejarlo dentro del agua.

words.en: Before releasing it we have to write down the time.
words.es: Antes de soltarlo hay que anotar la hora.

words.en: After putting the tag in, we have to write down the serial number.
words.es: Después de ponerle la marca, hay que anotar el número de serie.

words.en: Rodrigo, don't get near the bill; stay behind me.
words.es: Rodrigo, no te acerques al pico; quédate atrás de mí.
words.note: Informal (tú) with a friend.

words.en: Efraín, do you put the tag in or do I?
words.es: Efraín, ¿usted pone la marca o la pongo yo?
words.note: Formal (usted) with the mate.

words.en: Can you read this box to me, please?
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Read the serial number out loud, please.
words.es: Lee el número de serie en voz alta, por favor.
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Without taking it out of the water, how long do you think it is?
words.es: Sin sacarlo del agua, ¿cuánto crees que mide?

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Rodrigo, your friend: read the tag card aloud with la tarjeta dice que, explain the order with antes de and después de + infinitive and hay que, and check that he knows to keep the fish in the water and stay clear of the bill.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de soltarlo hay que anotar la hora; la tarjeta dice que...)

examples.es: Antes de marcarlo, hay que tener el aplicador listo.
examples.en: Before tagging it, we need to have the applicator ready.

examples.es: Después de anotar la hora, la tarjeta dice que hay que poner las coordenadas.
examples.en: After writing down the time, the card says we have to fill in the coordinates.

lessons.title: The Cruiser in the Photos Is in the Shop Today
lessons.objective: Find out what went wrong with the booked boat and propose a plan that works for your whole group.

words.note: Mexican marinas usually call a charter cruiser a yate, even a small one.
Mexican usage; Spain says la reserva.
Common Mexican word; you also hear protector solar.

words.en: What happened to the cruiser we booked?
words.es: ¿Qué le pasó al yate que reservamos?

words.en: In the photos, the cruiser had a cabin and a restroom.
words.es: En las fotos, el yate tenía cabina y baño.
words.note: Imperfect tenía describes how things were.

words.en: Yesterday you confirmed to me that everything was ready.
words.es: Ayer usted me confirmó que todo estaba listo.
words.note: Formal. Preterite for the event, imperfect for the state.

words.en: My father is 70 and can't take that much sun.
words.es: Mi papá tiene 70 años y no aguanta tanto sol.

words.en: Could you get us another boat with a shade top and a restroom?
words.es: ¿Podría conseguirnos otra embarcación con toldo y baño?
words.note: Formal, for the operator.

words.en: If there's no other boat, we'd prefer the full refund.
words.es: Si no hay otro barco, preferiríamos el reembolso completo.

words.en: Dad, would you be up for going on a panga if it has shade?
words.es: Papá, ¿te animarías a ir en panga si tiene sombra?
words.note: Informal, with family.

lessons.speaking: You are the group organizer, and the AI is Héctor, the marina operator: ask what happened to the booked cruiser using the preterite and imperfect (estaba, se descompuso), explain your father's needs, and propose a plan with ¿podríamos...? and ¿podría...?

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (el barco estaba listo, pero anoche se rompió; ¿podríamos...?)

examples.es: El yate estaba listo ayer, pero anoche se descompuso.
examples.en: The cruiser was ready yesterday, but last night it broke down.

examples.es: ¿Podríamos salir mañana en otro yate?
examples.en: Could we go out tomorrow on another cruiser?

lessons.title: No Sardines Today: Planning the Day on Artificials
lessons.objective: Compare the options without live bait and agree on a new plan for the day with your captain.

words.note: Anglers usually say it in the plural: vamos a probar plumas.
Standard loanword among Mexican anglers.

words.en: So, are we going to try feathers first?
Which of the three plans has the best chances?
words.es: ¿Cuál de los tres planes tiene más posibilidades?

words.en: With feathers we cover more water than with the jig.
words.es: Con plumas cubrimos más agua que con el jig.

words.en: That zone is farther, but there will be more dorado.
words.es: Esa zona está más lejos, pero habrá más dorado.

words.en: How much more are we going to spend on gas?
words.es: ¿Cuánto más vamos a gastar en gasolina?

words.en: Captain, you know the bay better than I do; what would you do?
words.es: Capitán, usted conoce la bahía mejor que yo; ¿qué haría?
words.note: Formal, for the captain.

words.en: If nothing bites by 10, we'll change zones.
words.es: Si a las 10 no pica nada, cambiaremos de zona.

words.en: I prefer plan two; it's better than waiting for bait.
words.es: Prefiero el plan dos; es mejor que esperar carnada.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Captain Toño: listen to his three plans without live bait, compare them with más... que and mejor que, and agree on the day's plan using vamos a and the future (probaremos, cambiaremos).

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (vamos a probar plumas; la sardina es más efectiva que el señuelo, pero...)

examples.es: Vamos a probar plumas mientras sale el sol.
examples.en: We're going to try feathers while the sun comes up.

examples.es: La sardina es mejor que el popper, pero hoy saldremos sin ella.
examples.en: Sardines are better than the popper, but today we'll go out without them.

lessons.title: A Tournament Observer Steps Aboard Mid-Fight
lessons.objective: Narrate a strike, fight and release to a tournament observer with exact times and numbers.

words.note: A man is el observador.

words.en: It struck at 9:42 on the starboard outrigger.
words.es: Picó a las 9:42 en el tangón de estribor.

words.en: We fought it 28 minutes and it jumped 4 times.
The mate touched the leader at 10:08.
words.es: El marinero tocó el líder a las 10:08.

words.en: When it struck, we were 8 miles from port.
words.es: Cuando picó, estábamos a 8 millas del puerto.

words.en: Sorry, could you repeat the question, please?
words.es: Perdón, ¿me repite la pregunta, por favor?
words.note: Formal, for the observer.

words.en: Hang on a sec, Chuy, I'm answering the observer.
words.es: Espérame tantito, Chuy, le contesto a la observadora.
words.note: Informal, to the mate; tantito is very Mexican.

words.en: Do you want to see the video of the jump?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Irene Vázquez, the tournament observer: narrate the strike, fight and release in order with the preterite (picó, peleamos, lo soltamos), giving exact times, minutes and your position.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (picó a las 9:42, peleamos veintiocho minutos, lo soltamos a las 10:10)

examples.es: Mi esposa tomó la caña a las 9:43 y peleó sola.
examples.en: My wife took the rod at 9:43 and fought it on her own.

examples.es: Lo soltamos a las 10:10 y se fue nadando bien.
examples.en: We released it at 10:10 and it swam off strong.

lessons.title: Saying No to a Trip When the Port Is Closed
lessons.objective: Refuse an off-the-books trip during a port closure and explain why to an eager friend.

words.note: In the Gulf and Caribbean, un norte is a strong north wind from a cold front.
Pirata is the everyday Mexican word for anything unlicensed.

words.en: No, thanks, we're not going out with the port closed.
words.es: No, gracias, no vamos a salir con el puerto cerrado.

words.en: Thanks, but I already told you no; please don't insist.
words.es: Gracias, pero ya le dije que no; no insista, por favor.
words.note: Formal, firm but polite, for Beto.

words.en: Daniel, don't give him money; that boat has no clearance.
words.es: Daniel, no le des dinero; esa lancha no tiene zarpe.
words.note: Informal, to your friend.

words.en: I don't recommend you get on an unlicensed boat.
words.es: No recomiendo que te subas a una lancha pirata.
words.note: No recomiendo que takes the subjunctive: te subas.

words.en: If something happens, there's no insurance and no one to rescue us.
words.es: Si pasa algo, no hay seguro ni nadie que nos rescate.

words.en: What does the Port Authority notice say for tomorrow?
words.es: ¿Qué dice el aviso de la capitanía para mañana?

words.en: Don't be mad, Daniel; when they open the port, we'll go out.
words.es: No te enojes, Daniel; cuando abran el puerto, salimos.
words.note: Cuando + subjunctive (abran) for a future event.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI plays Beto, a dockside hustler, and your friend Daniel: turn down Beto's cash trip firmly, then explain to Daniel why, using negative commands (no le des, no te subas) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no salgas, no recomiendo que salgamos con el puerto cerrado)

examples.es: No salgas hoy, Daniel; el puerto está cerrado por el norte.
examples.en: Don't go out today, Daniel; the port is closed because of the norther.

examples.es: No recomiendo que salgamos con el puerto cerrado.
examples.en: I don't recommend that we go out with the port closed.

lessons.title: Feedback for Lucía After She Lines Three Roosterfish
lessons.objective: Give kind, specific feedback on a friend's casting and recommend what she does on the next fish.

words.note: Use it to praise something done right: eso fue un acierto.
Fly anglers also say el loop.
Mexico says lentes; gafas is Spain.
delante del pez = in front of the fish.

words.en: Lucía, your loop looks really good, honestly.
words.es: Lucía, tu bucle se ve muy bien, de veras.
words.note: Informal. Start with specific praise before the correction.

words.en: The problem was that the fly landed on top of them.
words.es: El problema fue que la mosca cayó encima de ellos.

words.en: For the next one, I want you to cast farther ahead and off to the side.
words.es: Para el próximo, quiero que lances más adelante y a un lado.
words.note: Querer que + subjunctive: lances, not lanzas.

words.en: I suggest you strip fast as soon as you see it coming.
words.es: Te sugiero que recojas rápido en cuanto lo veas venir.
words.note: Recoger changes g to j: recojas.

words.en: I don't want you to get discouraged; it happens to almost all of us.
words.es: No quiero que te desanimes; a casi todos nos pasa.

words.en: Hopefully the next one comes closer to the shore.
words.es: Ojalá que el siguiente se acerque más a la orilla.
words.note: Ojalá (que) always takes the subjunctive.

words.en: Relax your wrist and let the rod do the work.
words.es: Relaja la muñeca y deja que la caña haga el trabajo.
words.note: Dejar que + subjunctive: haga.

words.en: Nacho, what do you recommend she change?
words.es: Nacho, ¿usted qué le recomienda que cambie?
words.note: Formal, to the guide.

lessons.speaking: You are Lucía's friend, and the AI is Lucía, with beach guide Nacho nearby: praise one specific thing she did well, then recommend changes for the next fish using quiero que lances..., te recomiendo que... and ojalá que...

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (quiero que lances delante, te recomiendo que esperes)

examples.es: Quiero que lances delante del pez gallo, no encima.
examples.en: I want you to cast in front of the roosterfish, not on top of it.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que esperes a que se acerque más.
examples.en: I recommend you wait until it comes closer.

lessons.title: Whose Marlin? Settling a Rod-Rotation Dispute
lessons.objective: Report what each person and the captain said and settle a dispute over the rod rotation.

words.note: In Mexico, a quarrel between people, not only a lawsuit.
Mexican: echar un volado = to flip a coin.

words.en: The captain said the turn changed after every strike.
words.es: El capitán dijo que el turno cambiaba después de cada picada.
words.note: Reported speech: dijo que + imperfect.

words.en: Pablo, you said it was your turn, right?
words.es: Pablo, tú dijiste que era tu turno, ¿verdad?
words.note: Informal, between friends.

words.en: Samuel, you were at the bow when it struck, right?
words.es: Samuel, tú estabas en la proa cuando picó, ¿no?
words.note: Imperfect for the background (estabas), preterite for the event (picó).

words.en: When it struck, Pablo was closer to the fighting chair.
words.es: Cuando picó, Pablo estaba más cerca de la silla de pelea.

words.en: Captain Medina, did you tell us the rotation was fixed?
words.es: Capitán Medina, ¿usted nos dijo que la rotación era fija?
words.note: Formal, to the captain.

words.en: Nobody is to blame; it was a misunderstanding.
words.es: Nadie tiene la culpa; fue un malentendido.

words.en: The fair thing is for Samuel to fight the next one.
words.es: Lo justo es que Samuel pelee el siguiente.

words.en: Next time, we flip a coin before we head out.
words.es: Para la próxima, echamos un volado antes de salir.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are the friend settling it, and the AI plays Pablo and Samuel at the marina: ask each what happened, report what Captain Medina said using el capitán dijo que... and the imperfect (estaba..., cuando picó), then propose a fair fix.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Pablo dijo que era su turno; Samuel estaba en el baño cuando picó)

examples.es: Pablo dijo que le tocaba a él porque Samuel no estaba.
examples.en: Pablo said it was his turn because Samuel wasn't there.

examples.es: Samuel estaba preparando un líder cuando picó el marlín.
examples.en: Samuel was rigging a leader when the marlin struck.

lessons.title: Keeping the Group Up on a Fishless Third Day
lessons.objective: Lift a discouraged group's spirits and commit to concrete changes for the last fishing day.

words.note: ¡Ánimo! on its own means cheer up.

words.en: Cheer up! Tomorrow we'll leave an hour earlier.
words.note: Future for a firm commitment: saldremos.

words.en: We're going to make it; this happens to anyone.
words.es: Lo vamos a lograr; esto le pasa a cualquiera.

words.en: Verónica, you cast really well yesterday; tomorrow it'll be your turn.
words.es: Verónica, ayer lanzaste muy bien; mañana te tocará a ti.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Iván, don't lose hope; our luck is going to change.
words.es: Iván, no te desesperes; la suerte va a cambiar.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Ramón, do you think there will be more action at the island?
words.es: Ramón, ¿usted cree que en la isla habrá más movimiento?
words.note: Formal, to the guide.

words.en: We'll try another technique: we'll fish the bottom with a jig.
words.es: Probaremos otra técnica: pescaremos al fondo con jig.

words.en: I'll take care of the bait and the ice.
words.es: Yo me encargaré de la carnada y del hielo.

words.en: Whatever happens, we'll have a good time tomorrow.
words.es: Pase lo que pase, mañana la pasaremos bien.

lessons.speaking: You are the group leader, and the AI plays Verónica, Iván and guide Ramón at the palapa: lift their spirits with ánimo and lo vamos a lograr, then agree on concrete changes for tomorrow using the future (saldremos, probaremos, me encargaré).

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (mañana saldremos más temprano; lo vamos a lograr, ánimo)

examples.es: Mañana saldremos más temprano y pescaremos cerca de la isla.
examples.en: Tomorrow we'll leave earlier and fish near the island.

examples.es: Ánimo, lo vamos a lograr; Ramón conoce bien estas aguas.
examples.en: Cheer up, we're going to make it; Ramón knows these waters well.

lessons.title: One Release Plan, Four Listeners
lessons.objective: Explain one release plan to an owner, a guide and a teenager, switching register, and check each version.

words.note: Common name for permit in the Mexican Caribbean.
Hule is Mexican for rubber.
anzuelo sin rebaba = barbless hook.

words.en: Doña Carmen, I'd like to explain how we'll release the permit.
words.es: Doña Carmen, quisiera explicarle cómo vamos a soltar las palometas.
words.note: Formal. Quisiera softens the request.

words.en: Could you repeat it back to me in your own words, please?
words.es: ¿Podría usted repetírmelo con sus palabras, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Could you share the procedure with the other guides?
words.es: ¿Podría usted compartir el procedimiento con los otros guías?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Sorry, Gilberto, I forgot: I'll use tú with you.
words.es: Perdón, Gilberto, se me olvidó: te hablo de tú.
words.note: Hablar de tú / de usted = to use tú / usted.

words.en: Gilberto, how about we use the rubber net?
words.es: Gilberto, ¿te parece si usamos la red de hule?
words.note: Informal softener.

words.en: I'd like to ask you all to use only barbless hooks.
words.es: Quisiera pedirles que solo usen anzuelos sin rebaba.
words.note: Pedir que + subjunctive: usen.

words.en: Kevin, don't take it out of the water; wet your hands first.
words.es: Kevin, no la saques del agua; mójate las manos primero.
words.note: Informal, to the teen.

words.en: Kevin, okay, explain the plan to me as if I didn't know it.
words.es: Kevin, a ver, explícame el plan como si yo no lo supiera.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are the visiting angler, and the AI plays Doña Carmen, guide Gilberto and his nephew Kevin: explain your permit-release plan to each, using usted with softeners (quisiera pedirle, ¿podría usted...?) or tú (¿te parece si...?), and have each say it back.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera pedirle, ¿podría usted...?, ¿te parece si...?)

examples.es: Doña Carmen, ¿podría usted revisar el plan conmigo?
examples.en: Doña Carmen, could you go over the plan with me?

examples.es: Gilberto, ¿te parece si soltamos la palometa en el bajo?
examples.en: Gilberto, how about we release the permit on the flat?

lessons.title: A Treble Hook in the Hand: Timeline for the Clinic
lessons.objective: Give a clinic a clear timeline of a hook injury and what was done on the boat, without guessing at treatment.

words.note: Often shortened to la antitetánica in Mexico.
Use la doctora for a woman; address her as doctora.

words.en: At 10:15 the hook went into his palm.
words.es: A las 10:15 se le clavó el anzuelo en la palma.

words.en: While the mate was separating the lure, I held his hand still.
words.es: Mientras el marinero separaba el señuelo, yo le sostenía la mano.
words.note: Imperfect for the ongoing background action after mientras.

words.en: We didn't try to take the hook out on the boat.
words.es: No intentamos sacarle el anzuelo en la panga.

words.en: Half an hour later, we were already heading back to port.
words.es: Media hora después, ya íbamos de regreso al puerto.

words.en: When we reached the dock, we took a taxi to the clinic.
words.es: Al llegar al muelle, tomamos un taxi a la clínica.

words.en: I don't know if his tetanus shot is up to date.
words.es: No sé si tiene la vacuna del tétanos al día.

words.en: Doctor, the treatment is your decision; I'm just telling you what happened.
words.es: Doctora, el tratamiento lo decide usted; yo solo le cuento.
words.note: Formal: usted with the doctor.

words.en: Tomás, easy, the doctor is coming.
words.es: Tomás, tranquilo, la doctora ya viene.
words.note: Informal: tú with your friend.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Dr. Elena Moreno at the clinic: give her a clear timeline of Tomás's hook injury and what the mate did on the boat, using a las..., media hora después, mientras... and al llegar, and leave every treatment decision to her.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las diez, media hora después, mientras el marinero..., al llegar al muelle)

examples.es: A las 10:15 el pez se sacudió y el anzuelo se le clavó.
examples.en: At 10:15 the fish thrashed and the hook went into him.

examples.es: Al llegar al muelle, la mano ya estaba hinchada.
examples.en: When we reached the dock, his hand was already swollen.

lessons.title: Near Miss: A Wrapped Line on a Big Yellowfin
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss without blame, saying what almost happened and what changes next time.

words.en: The line almost wrapped around his hand.
words.es: Por poco se le enreda la línea en la mano.
words.note: Por poco + present tense tells a past event that almost happened.

words.en: He could have cut his fingers with that braid.
words.es: Podría haberse cortado los dedos con esa trenza.

words.en: Something serious almost happened, but we're not looking for someone to blame.
words.es: Casi pasa algo grave, pero aquí no buscamos culpables.

words.en: Ethan, I know you wanted to help; I'm not angry.
words.es: Ethan, sé que querías ayudar; no estoy enojado.
words.note: Informal: tú with your nephew.

words.en: Joel, what would you change for next time?
words.es: Joel, ¿qué cambiaría usted para la próxima vez?
words.note: Formal: usted with the mate.

words.en: If it happens again, only the mate touches the line.
words.es: Si vuelve a pasar, solo el marinero toca la línea.

words.en: If the line is running, everyone steps away from the reel.
words.es: Si la línea corre, todos se alejan del carrete.

words.en: Ethan, if you want to help, tell me first.
words.es: Ethan, si quieres ayudar, avísame primero.
words.note: Informal command: avísame.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is mate Joel Arce: talk through Ethan's near miss with the running line without blaming anyone, saying what almost happened with por poco, casi and podría haber, and agree on a deck rule using si vuelve a pasar...

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco se le enreda; podría haberse cortado; si vuelve a pasar, ...)

examples.es: Por poco se le enreda la línea en la muñeca durante la corrida.
examples.en: The line almost wrapped around his wrist during the run.

examples.es: Si vuelve a pasar, nadie agarra la línea con la mano.
examples.en: If it happens again, nobody grabs the line by hand.

lessons.title: Fuel Smell in the Bilge: Calling It and Heading In
lessons.objective: Report a fuel smell, agree to head in, and give short, clear phone updates to the outfitter's office.

words.en: Captain, it smells like gasoline in the bilge.
words.es: Capitán, huele a gasolina en la sentina.
words.note: Huele a + noun: it smells like.

words.en: Nobody smokes; put out that cigarette now.
words.es: Nadie fuma; apaguen ese cigarro ya.
words.note: Plural ustedes command to the group.

words.en: If the smell continues, we'll head back to port.
words.es: Si sigue el olor, regresaremos al puerto.

words.en: It's your call, captain; we agree on heading in.
words.es: Usted decide, capitán; estamos de acuerdo en regresar.
words.note: Formal: usted with the captain.

words.en: Sandra, I'm calling you from Captain Lalo's boat.
words.es: Sandra, le hablo desde la panga del capitán Lalo.
words.note: Formal: le hablo is the usual Mexican way to say I'm calling you.

words.en: Can you send us a mechanic and a van to the dock?
words.es: ¿Nos puede mandar un mecánico y una camioneta al muelle?

words.en: We'll arrive in 40 minutes if the sea stays calm.
words.es: Llegaremos en 40 minutos si el mar sigue tranquilo.

words.en: If the call drops, I'll send you a text.
words.es: Si se corta la llamada, le mandaré un mensaje.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Captain Lalo Quiroz and then Sandra Félix at the outfitter's office: report the gasoline smell, back the call to head in, and give short phone updates using si + present → future and short commands like nadie fuma.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si sigue el olor, regresaremos; nadie fuma, apaguen eso)

examples.es: Si el olor aumenta, el capitán apagará el motor.
examples.en: If the smell gets stronger, the captain will shut off the engine.

examples.es: Si no hay señal, la llamaré desde el muelle.
examples.en: If there's no signal, I'll call you from the dock.

lessons.title: A Fisheries Inspector Checks the Catch at the Dock
lessons.objective: Answer a fisheries inspector formally and follow the inspection procedure for permits and catch.

words.note: Acta is feminine but takes el in the singular: el acta, las actas.
Formal word for each fish in official procedures.

words.en: Good afternoon, inspector; here are my license and my ID.
words.es: Buenas tardes, inspector; aquí tiene mi licencia y mi identificación.
words.note: Formal throughout: usted.

words.en: May I see your ID badge, please?
words.es: ¿Me permite ver su credencial, por favor?

words.en: We have three yellowtail in the cooler; you may check them.
words.es: Llevamos tres jureles de Castilla en la hielera; puede revisarlos.

words.en: How is each fish measured under the regulation?
words.es: ¿Cómo se mide cada ejemplar según la norma?

words.en: Excuse me, what goes in the remarks box?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿qué se anota en la casilla de observaciones?

words.en: May I read the report before I sign it?
words.es: ¿Me permite leer el acta antes de firmarla?

words.en: Sorry, I don't understand this part; could you explain it to me?
words.es: Perdón, no entiendo esta parte; ¿me la explica, por favor?

words.en: Could you give me a copy of the report, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede dar una copia del acta, por favor?

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is CONAPESCA inspector Arturo Salgado at the Ensenada pier: answer him formally with usted, hand over your documents, ask how the procedure works using passive se (se revisan, se mide), and read his form before you sign.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se revisan los permisos, se mide cada pez según la norma que cita el inspector)

examples.es: Primero se revisan los permisos y luego se abre la hielera.
examples.en: First the permits are checked, and then the cooler is opened.

examples.es: Se mide cada jurel de Castilla según la norma que cita el inspector.
examples.en: Each yellowtail is measured according to the regulation the inspector cites.

lessons.title: Write the Tag Report for the Sailfish We Released
lessons.objective: Write a clear, formal tag report email and answer the coordinator's follow-up question.

words.note: Used for a woman; for a man, say el coordinador.
Standard formal email closing, placed right before your name.
Pronounced 'ge pe ese'.

words.en: Dear Dr. Ibarra: I am sending you the report on the tagged sailfish.
words.es: Estimada Dra. Ibarra: le envío el informe del pez vela marcado.
words.note: Formal. Dra. is short for doctora, and a colon follows the greeting.

words.en: First of all, the sailfish struck at 8:15.
words.es: En primer lugar, el pez vela picó a las 8:15.

words.en: Subsequently, the tag was placed in the dorsal muscle.
words.es: Posteriormente, se colocó la marca en el músculo dorsal.
words.note: Impersonal se is typical of written reports.

words.en: It should be noted that the fish never left the water.
words.es: Cabe señalar que el pez nunca salió del agua.

words.en: Finally, it was released and swam off strongly.
words.es: Por último, se liberó y se fue nadando con fuerza.

words.en: I am attaching the photo of the card with the serial number.
words.es: Le adjunto la foto de la tarjeta con el número de serie.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Sorry for the omission; I am sending the missing data point below.
words.es: Disculpe la omisión; le envío el dato faltante a continuación.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I remain available for any questions or clarification.
words.es: Quedo atento a cualquier duda o aclaración.
words.note: Women write atenta. This is a standard formal closing line.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler, and the AI is Dr. Paola Ibarra, the tagging coordinator: write your formal tag report on the released sailfish and answer her follow-up, using en primer lugar, posteriormente, cabe señalar que and por último.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, posteriormente, cabe señalar que, por último)

examples.es: En primer lugar, salimos del muelle de Zihuatanejo a las 6:30.
examples.en: First of all, we left the Zihuatanejo dock at 6:30.

examples.es: Por último, cabe señalar que Rodrigo grabó la liberación en video.
examples.en: Finally, it should be noted that Rodrigo recorded the release on video.

lessons.title: Texts and Calls: Moving Tomorrow's Charter for a North Wind
lessons.objective: Move a booking by text and phone, leave a clear voice message, and accept a polite counteroffer.

words.note: In Mexico, WhatsApp voice notes are usually called audios.
¿Hay cupo? = Is there room? This is very common in Mexico.
Gracias de antemano = thanks in advance. It is common in polite texts.

words.en: Hi, Marisol, would it be possible to change tomorrow's trip?
words.es: Hola, Marisol, ¿sería posible cambiar el viaje de mañana?
words.note: The conditional sería softens the request in a text.

words.en: Good afternoon, Marisol, I'm calling about the tarpon trip.
words.es: Buenas tardes, Marisol, le llamo por el viaje de sábalo.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'd like to move it to the day after tomorrow, if there's room.
words.es: Me gustaría moverlo a pasado mañana, si hay cupo.

words.en: I would appreciate it if you confirmed it by text.
words.es: Le agradecería que me lo confirmara por mensaje.
words.note: Formal. Le agradecería que + imperfect subjunctive (confirmara).

words.en: Sorry, it cut out; can you hear me well now?
words.es: Perdón, se cortó; ¿me escucha bien ahora?
words.note: Formal.
In voice messages, read numbers in pairs or small groups.

words.en: A half day on the lagoon sounds good; what time do we leave?
words.es: Me parece bien medio día en la laguna; ¿a qué hora salimos?

words.en: Thank you very much for the alternative, I really appreciate it.
words.es: Muchas gracias por la alternativa, de veras se lo agradezco.
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the angler on Holbox, and the AI is outfitter Marisol Canul: text and call to move tomorrow's tarpon trip, leave a clear voice message and agree on a new plan, using ¿sería posible…?, me gustaría and le agradecería.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿sería posible cambiarlo?, me gustaría, le agradecería)

examples.es: ¿Sería posible cambiar el viaje de sábalo para el jueves?
examples.en: Would it be possible to change the tarpon trip to Thursday?

examples.es: Me gustaría saber si hay cupo en la laguna pasado mañana.
examples.en: I would like to know if there's room on the lagoon the day after tomorrow.

lessons.title: Final Debrief With the Outfitter: Next Season's Terms
lessons.objective: Review the week honestly with the outfitter and rebook next season on clear conditions.

words.note: Used for a man; for a woman, say la gerente.
¡Trato hecho! = It's a deal! The word also means treatment.
This is a common Mexican way to say next year.
When it means 'as long as', use the subjunctive after it: siempre que tenga.
Always followed by the subjunctive: con tal de que salgamos.

words.en: Óscar, in all honesty, Tuesday's delay cost us the morning.
words.es: Óscar, con toda honestidad, el retraso del martes nos costó la mañana.
words.note: Formal (usted) with the lodge manager, but on a first-name basis.

words.en: The sailfish release was the best part of the week.
words.es: La liberación del pez vela fue lo mejor de la semana.

words.en: I'd come back without hesitating, as long as the boat has shade.
words.es: Volvería sin dudarlo, siempre que el barco tenga sombra.

words.en: I'd book the same dates provided that we leave on time.
words.es: Reservaría las mismas fechas con tal de que salgamos a tiempo.

words.en: Could you guarantee the same crew if I book now?
words.es: ¿Podrían garantizar la misma tripulación si reservo ahora?

words.en: I'd leave the deposit today, as long as it's refundable.
words.es: Dejaría el depósito hoy, siempre que sea reembolsable.

words.en: That seems fair; so, it's a deal!
Would it be all right with you if we put it all in writing?
words.es: ¿Le parecería bien que lo pongamos todo por escrito?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the guest, and the AI is Óscar Benítez, the lodge manager: review the week honestly, good and bad, then rebook next season on clear terms with the conditional (volvería, reservaría) and siempre que or con tal de que plus the subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (volvería siempre que el barco tenga sombra; con tal de que salgamos a tiempo)

examples.es: Volvería el año que entra siempre que nos toque el mismo capitán.
examples.en: I would come back next year as long as we get the same captain.

examples.es: Óscar, firmaríamos hoy con tal de que el desayuno esté listo a las 5:30.
examples.en: Óscar, we would sign today provided that breakfast is ready at 5:30.

lessons.title: Capstone: Leading a Group's Full Day Out of Buena Vista
lessons.objective: Lead a group through a full day of plans, problems, safety calls, reports and thanks, all in Spanish.

words.note: For a woman, la líder del grupo.
Plática is the everyday Mexican word for a talk or briefing.

words.en: Put on your life jackets and listen to Captain Chema, please.
words.es: Pónganse el chaleco y escuchen al capitán Chema, por favor.
words.note: Ustedes commands to the group, with the personal a before the captain (al capitán).

words.en: Captain, if there are no sardines, what lures would you recommend?
words.es: Capitán, si no hay sardina, ¿qué señuelos nos recomendaría?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Graciela, keep the line tight and let the drag do the work.
words.es: Graciela, mantén la línea tensa y deja que el freno trabaje.
words.note: Informal (tú) with a friend.

words.en: Andrés, step away from the reel; only Chema touches the line.
words.es: Andrés, aléjate del carrete; la línea solo la toca Chema.
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: That was close; let's talk about it now so it doesn't happen again.
words.es: Estuvo cerca; lo hablamos ahora para que no se repita.

words.en: Captain, if the wind keeps picking up, I'd rather we head back now.
words.es: Capitán, si el viento sigue subiendo, prefiero que regresemos ya.
words.note: Formal. Prefiero que + subjunctive (regresemos).

words.en: Good afternoon, just letting you know we're coming back early because of the wind.
words.es: Buenas tardes, le aviso que regresamos antes por el viento.
words.note: Formal text to the outfitter.

words.en: In summary, it was a good day and we all came back safe.
words.es: En resumen, fue un buen día y todos regresamos a salvo.

lessons.speaking: You are leading the day, and the AI is Captain Chema and your friends Graciela and Andrés: brief the group with ustedes commands, plan with Chema in formal usted, coach a fight, make safety calls with si clauses and the subjunctive, then text the outfitter and write the day's log.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar (connectors, commands, subjunctive, conditional, si clauses, formal and written register)

examples.es: Si el viento sube antes de la hora límite, regresaremos sin discutir.
examples.en: If the wind picks up before the turnaround time, we will head back without arguing.

examples.es: Posteriormente, cabe señalar que Andrés se alejó del carrete a tiempo.
examples.en: Subsequently, it should be noted that Andrés stepped away from the reel in time.
